newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines cuts power rates in most grids.
newsitem.headline: Philippines cuts power rates in most grids.

text.p: The state-owned National Power Corp (Napocor) of the Philippines said on Friday it is reducing power rates by 6.98 centavos per kilowatt-hour (kwh) in the northern island of Luzon effective today.

Napocor president Guido A. Delgado told reporters that the reduction was brought about by lower costs of power from power plants operated by private companies as well as the appreciation of the peso against the U.S. dollar.

The rate adjustment will take effect from December 27 to January 26. Napocor adjusts its rates monthly depending on the cost of fuel and power purchased from privately-operated power plants as well as the foreign exchange rate.
Napocor will also cut rates in the Leyte-Samar grid in the central Philippines by 6.88 centavos per kwh and in the southern Mindanao island by 2.56 centavos per kwh.

But electricity rates will be raised by 0.57 centavos in the central provinces of Cebu, Negros and Panay and in Bohol province in central Visayas island by 12.09 centavos per kwh due to higher costs of fuel in the areas.
